This sum is defined as a Wishart distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom and a (matrix) parameter $ $. Recalling that the sum of $n$ squared unit normals follows a $ _n^2$ distribution, the Wishart is the extension to the multivariate normal. The Wishart is the sampling distribution for covariance matrices (just like the $ ^ 2 $ is associated with the distribution of a sample variance for data drawn from a normal; Chapter 11). The pdf of the Wishart distribution is $$ p(\mathbf{W}\mid\mathbf{V})=2^{-n k/2}\pi^{-k(k-1)/k}\mid\mathbf{V}\mid^{-n/2}\mid\mathbf{W}\mid^{(n+k+1)/2}\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{t}\mathbf{r}\left[\mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{W}\right]\right)}{\prod_{i=1}^{k}\Gamma\left(\frac{n+1-i}{2}\right)} $$
